Every graph/vector/keyword question below was actually run against the live corpus this session (retrieval/graph_retriever.py, retrieval/vector_retriever.py, retrieval/keyword_retriever.py); hybrid questions are compositional by nature and are noted as such rather than independently retrievable by one primitive.

known_gaps_this_pass_confirmed: No fulltext index covers Chunk body text or full document text (document_fulltext only indexes Paper/Markdown title+description) — literal in-text substring search is not possible today (Q10).
Paper.arxiv_id was never populated at ingestion (both Papers' arxiv_id property is None) — exact arXiv-id lookup is not possible today via any index (Q11).

Lucene scores are not comparable across different fulltext indexes (field length/index characteristics differ) — merging top-k-per-index by raw score can bury a strong single-index hit under numerically larger but less relevant hits from another index (seen while checking Q11 with 'Knowledge Graphs'). Relevant to Step 10E fusion design, not fixed here.
Graph retrieval (retrieval/graph_retriever.py) is 1-hop by construction — only AUTHORED_BY/MENTIONS are domain relationship types (docs/architecture.md §12.10).
fixed_this_pass: organization_fulltext was missing (only document_fulltext/person_fulltext/technology_fulltext existed) — a real coverage gap, not a scoping choice, since Organization is the most common KnowledgeEntity label in this corpus. Added to graph/schema/indexes.cypher, applied, confirmed ONLINE. Q15 updated to reflect the corrected (now-passing) keyword result. See docs/architecture.md for the closed-gap note.
_meta.step_12_extension: Questions 17-23 added during the Step 12 (NL->Cypher) investigation and closeout. The investigation found the graph questions get_entity_context() genuinely can't express are a narrow, enumerable class (composed multi-call patterns and whole-graph aggregates), not evidence of open-ended query flexibility — see docs/architecture.md's Step 12 deferral entry. Questions 17-18 are composed-call patterns (2-3 get_entity_context() calls + Python set logic, zero new Cypher); 19-21 are served by the new graph/queries/aggregates.py fixed templates; 22-23 are deliberate calibration gaps (CITES: mechanically valid, zero data; USES: not in the schema at all), same treatment as question 14. Step 12 (LLM-generated Cypher + validation pipeline) itself was NOT built — deferred, reactivation condition documented in architecture.md.

questions.question: What does the rdflib repository depend on?
questions.notes: Deliberate gap/calibration question, not a bug to fix: USES (Repository->Technology) is formally deferred to Phase 3 (architecture.md §12.6 / 7A.3). Included so the Step 11 planner is built against a question it must correctly decline, not just ones it can answer. RELABELED (Step 11 scoping): the original retrieval_type="hybrid" conflated two different questions — which retriever should this be ROUTED to (graph — "depend on" is DEPENDS_ON/USES-shaped language, and the deterministic classifier correctly identifies it as such) versus whether the final ANSWER needs synthesis to explain why graph came back empty (yes, but that's the explainability/synthesis step's job, Step 13, not retrieval's). routing_type is the field the query classifier is scored against; retrieval_type is left as "hybrid" for continuity with how this question was originally framed as a calibration case, not because it's the correct routing target.

questions.question: What is ACL?
questions.notes: REVISED after adding organization_fulltext: originally keyword returned 0 results (Organization label had no fulltext index at all — a real coverage gap, not by design). With the index added, applied, and confirmed ONLINE, keyword now finds all 3 raw org_acl entities cleanly. It still does NOT surface the org_acl Canonical, even though Canonical:Organization carries the Organization label and is structurally in scope for the index: Canonical uses `canonical_name`, not `name`, and the index is defined on `name`/`description`/`aliases` — verified org_acl's Canonical has name=None, description=None, aliases=None, so it contributes nothing indexable. Vector name-search, by contrast, surfaces both the 3 raw entities AND the Canonical (all at score 1.0, exact-name match) because canonical_name_embedding is a separate index built specifically over Canonical.name_embedding. Net: keyword and vector now roughly agree on the raw-entity results, but only vector reaches the canonical — a genuine, still-standing capability difference worth keeping in the corpus, not the original all-or-nothing gap. REVISED AGAIN (Step 11 closing): the question text was originally a meta-instruction ("compare keyword search against vector name-search") written for Step 10F's own testing purposes, not a question a real user would ask — end-to-end routing testing showed this concretely, passing that meta-text into vector/keyword search returned nothing (the comparison language drowned out "ACL"). Reworded to "What is ACL?", a genuine natural-language question; the pipeline was not changed to accommodate the old phrasing. retrieval_type is left as the historical keyword_vs_vector_name label (this question's original purpose — contrasting the two search modes on the same target term — is still accurately described by it); routing_type is what the classifier/planner are scored against.

questions.question: Which papers does the Knowledge Graphs survey cite?
questions.notes: Step 12 investigation question 6 — calibration case, deliberately included. get_entity_context('paper_2003_02320v6_pdf', relationship_types=['CITES']) is a perfectly valid single filtered call (CITES IS a member of models.relationship.RELATIONSHIP_TYPES) and executes cleanly — it just returns [], because 0 CITES edges exist anywhere in the graph (confirmed via direct Cypher: MATCH ()-[r:CITES]->() RETURN count(r) is 0). This is a data/extraction gap (citation extraction was never built), not a retrieval-mechanism gap — distinguishes cleanly from question 23's schema gap below. No amount of query flexibility, generated or fixed, produces an answer here; only citation extraction would.

questions.question: What is the average confidence of USES relationships between repositories and the technologies they depend on?
questions.notes: Step 12 investigation question 7, re-verified against the new aggregate path (graph/queries/aggregates.py::relationship_type_stats), not just the original get_entity_context() finding. 'USES' is not a member of models.relationship.RELATIONSHIP_TYPES at all (confirmed empirically, both here and in question 14's notes) — physical.md documents a resource-level USES relationship in prose, but it was never added to the actual schema enum; 7A.3 is deferred to Phase 3 (architecture.md §12.6). relationship_type_stats() raises ValueError before ever reaching Neo4j, same as get_entity_context() would. Same underlying schema gap as question 14, approached through the new aggregate function instead of the graph retriever, to confirm the gap is consistent across both code paths, not just one.
